coverage.surface: Getting to Signed default screen (v4) — at rest, deal selected, ledger rows open, security coverage, signature plan, lessons input, copy actions, toasts
coverage.note: Read the whole component and its model; compared with the SMB walkthrough generated today (at rest with no deal, each SMB deal chosen, each ledger row opened, Show details, Mark it settled) and the enterprise walkthrough of 2026-11-06. Copy-to-clipboard text, toasts, the all-resolved empty state and keyboard/accessibility behaviour were reviewed from source only (the walkthrough does not capture clipboard or toast text).

findings.state: At rest with no deal selected (Business approval defaults to 'at risk'); and after 'Mark it settled' when the next open workstream is only 'to do'
findings.current: Current blocking issue  (followed by 'CUSTOMER REQUEST · BUSINESS APPROVAL' or 'CUSTOMER REQUEST · LEGAL')
findings.problem: pickBlocking() (fronts.ts:595-603) returns a 'blocking' workstream if one exists, otherwise an 'at risk' one, otherwise the first open one. The heading always says 'Current blocking issue', so a workstream marked 'to do' or 'at risk' is presented as the issue currently blocking the deal. SMB walkthrough at rest (no deal chosen, nothing entered) shows 'CURRENT BLOCKING ISSUE · CUSTOMER REQUEST · BUSINESS APPROVAL' while the same row's status reads 'AT RISK'; after 'Mark it settled' it shows LEGAL as the blocking issue while the Legal row reads 'TO DO'. Declarative certainty: a selection rule is stated as a fact about the deal.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (dimension 4, declarative certainty); ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/07_REWRITE_BATCH_02_STRATEGIC_AND_DIAGNOSTIC.md Getting to Signed structural requirement (status shown per workstream); original record B2-X-077 / HS-016 (replacement 'CURRENT BLOCKING ISSUE' assumed the item shown is actually blocking)
findings.proposed: Choose the heading from the selected workstream's status: `const head = face.status === "blocking" ? t("Current blocking issue") : face.status === "at_risk" ? t("Workstream at risk") : t("Next open workstream");` and render `{head}` at line 237.

findings.state: Any deal with no saved Getting to Signed state, and the screen with no deal selected
findings.current: business: { ...EMPTY_FRONT, status: "at_risk" }  → ledger row 'BUSINESS APPROVAL stakeholder engagement and the signature plan AT RISK'
findings.problem: Every new deal starts with Business approval marked 'at risk' although nothing about the deal has been recorded. A first-time user reads 'AT RISK' as an assessment of their deal (and, with GTS-001, as the current blocking issue). The status is a default, not evidence.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (dimension 4, declarative certainty); COPY_STANDARD.md §21 (claims never more certain than the data)
findings.proposed: Smallest accurate change without a product decision: when the business workstream is still at its default (status at_risk, empty theirAsk and yourLine), show the row hint as `t("stakeholder engagement and the signature plan · marked at risk until a signature plan is recorded", { class: "body" })` instead of the plain hint. OWNER DECISION: start Business approval at 'to do' (EMPTY_SIGNED_STATE.fronts.business = EMPTY_FRONT) so no status is asserted before the seller records anything; doctrine deliberately defaulted it to at-risk to keep the committee in view.

findings.state: Current-issue action row; button enabled once both customer request and proposed position are filled
findings.problem: The button does not send anything: it copies a drafted sentence to the clipboard (copyText, line 255-258) and the toast says 'Proposed response copied.' A first-time user expects a message to go to the customer. The wording is the approved Batch 02 replacement (B2-X-083) verbatim, but it misdescribes what the code does.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §21 (copy must not claim behaviour the product does not have); comprehension principle
findings.proposed: Change the label to `t("Copy proposed response →")`.

findings.state: Copied proposed-response text when the target signature date field is empty
findings.current: On {workstream}: you've asked for {request}. Our proposed position: {position}. Happy to walk through it — our current target signature date is month-end.
findings.problem: When no target date has been entered the template substitutes the placeholder 'month-end' as if it were the seller's agreed target, so the message the seller pastes to the customer states a date nobody set.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §21; ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/07_REWRITE_BATCH_02_STRATEGIC_AND_DIAGNOSTIC.md (target signature date is a recorded field, not an assumption)
findings.proposed: Only include the date clause when one was entered: `... ${t("Our proposed position:")} ${face.yourLine}. ${state.targetDate.trim() ? `${t("Happy to walk through it — our current target signature date is", { class: "body" })} ${state.targetDate.trim()}.` : t("Happy to walk through it.")}`

findings.state: Lessons for future deals: type a lesson and press Enter
findings.problem: The toast points to a 'deal-learning record' the user cannot find: the v4 screen never lists saved lessons, appendLearning (state.ts:141-150) stores them under gtmos_negotiation_learnings with negotiationId "draft" and no deal id, and no other area reads that key (grep finds no consumer outside src/getting-to-signed). The phrase is private ontology and implies the lesson is attached to the deal.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (dimensions 2 and 6); ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/07_REWRITE_BATCH_02_STRATEGIC_AND_DIAGNOSTIC.md row 'WE WON'T REPEAT THIS' → 'LESSONS FOR FUTURE DEALS' (lessons log)
findings.proposed: Toast `t("Lesson saved.")` and list the five most recent lessons under the input (`learnings.value.slice(0, 5)`, as the previous screen version already does in ds/components/RehearsalObject.tsx:521-527) so the user can see where it went. OWNER DECISION: store the deal id on each lesson and feed lessons to Future Autopsy / Founding GTM as the capability map describes ('a we-won't-repeat-this log feeding loss patterns').

findings.problem: The status list calls the same state 'resolved' (STATUS_LABEL.settled = 'resolved'; the row then shows 'RESOLVED'), so the button uses the internal key word while the status uses another. Two names for one state.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (consistent terms); ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/07_REWRITE_BATCH_02_STRATEGIC_AND_DIAGNOSTIC.md Getting to Signed (status per workstream)

findings.state: All four workstreams marked resolved (pickBlocking returns null)
findings.current: No workstream is currently marked as blocking. / If Legal, Security, Finance, and Business approval are settled, focus on completing the remaining signature steps.
findings.problem: This panel only renders when all four workstreams are resolved, yet the heading describes the state by absence ('no workstream … blocking') and the body hedges with 'If … are settled' about a condition the code already knows is true. It also uses 'settled' where the status label says 'resolved'.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §26 (don't describe something by its absence); comprehension principle (dimension 7)
findings.proposed: h3: `t("All four workstreams are marked resolved.")`; p: `t("Finish the remaining steps in the signature plan under Business approval.", { class: "body" })`

findings.state: Ledger row with a recorded customer request (both demo books)
findings.current: LEGAL Uncapped liability on candidate-data claims Uncapped liability on candidate-data claims→Cap at 12 months of fees …
findings.problem: When a request is recorded the row prints it twice: once in place of the workstream hint (line 282) and again before the arrow (line 285). The SMB walkthrough shows the duplication on every seeded row, and the button's accessible name repeats it.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (scanability); ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/original-working-set/07_REWRITE_BATCH_02_STRATEGIC_AND_DIAGNOSTIC.md row B2-X-087..090 (row = workstream · description · status)
findings.proposed: Always show the workstream description in the first line: `{FRONT_META[id].hint}`; keep the request → position line below it.

findings.state: Stakeholder chip for a person added without any recorded touch
findings.problem: engagementRead() returns band 'new' when lastTouch is null (fronts.ts:587-589). 'new' reads as 'newly added stakeholder', but it means no touch has been recorded; a stakeholder added months ago with no recorded touch still shows 'new'.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (dimension 1, semantic compression); COPY_STANDARD.md §17 (state names an observable condition)

findings.state: Stakeholder strip with at least one stakeholder
findings.current: <span class="gs4-chip" title="Record a new touch with this stakeholder" onClick=…>
findings.problem: Clicking a stakeholder chip records a touch (updates lastTouch and the engagement state), but the chip is a span with no role, tabindex or key handler, so the action is mouse-only and invisible to keyboard and screen-reader users; the only explanation is a hover title.
findings.governing: comprehension principle; COPY_STANDARD.md (actions are named); WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard
findings.proposed: Render the clickable part as `<button type="button" class="gs4-chip…" aria-label={`${t("Record a touch today with")} ${m.name}`}>` containing the dot, name and role, and move the remove button outside it (nested buttons are invalid).

findings.problem: Every stakeholder's remove button has the same accessible name ('Remove' via title, visible '×'), so a screen-reader user cannot tell which person it removes.
The four document buttons are toggles but expose no aria-pressed, so assistive technology cannot tell which documents are marked available; only a CSS class changes.

findings.state: Security workstream open; type a number into 'answered by existing documents' larger than 'questions total'
findings.problem: Live input is not clamped to the total, so the bar can show e.g. '45 covered' of 40 with 0 open until reload, when parseState clamps it (fronts.ts:528). The displayed coverage can contradict the total the user entered.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (numbers must agree with their formula)
findings.proposed: Clamp on input: `covered: Math.min(Number(value) || 0, cov.total)` and re-clamp `covered` when `total` is lowered.

findings.state: Security coverage summary with exactly one open question or one saved answer
findings.current: Of the 1 open questions, 1 have saved answers; 0 still need input from the appropriate technical owner.
findings.problem: The sentence is assembled from fixed plural fragments, so singular counts read ungrammatically.
findings.proposed: Choose singular/plural forms: `covOpen === 1 ? t("open question,") : t("open questions,")` and `saved === 1 ? t("has a saved answer;") : t("have saved answers;")`, likewise 'still needs'/'still need'.

findings.state: Workstream ledger (all rows) — structure required by Batch 02
findings.current: Each workstream records only customer request, proposed position and status; owner, next action and due date are not captured per workstream.
findings.problem: Batch 02 requires each workstream to show 'customer request, your proposed position, gap, status, owner, next action, and due date'. Owners and dates exist only as free text in the single signature-plan box under Business approval, so a seller cannot see who owns the Security or Legal workstream or when the next step is due.
findings.proposed: Smallest change without a product decision: make the signature-plan heading say it holds owners and dates for every workstream: `t("Signature plan · dated steps and named owners for every workstream", { class: "body" })`. OWNER DECISION: add owner, next action and due date fields to each workstream (additive optional fields on the stored Front shape; no migration needed because parseFront defaults missing fields).

findings.state: Deal selected — deal value link next to the account name
findings.problem: The link's only text is a decorative diamond and an amount, so neither sighted users nor screen readers are told it opens the deal in Deal Workspace.
findings.proposed: Add `title` and `aria-label={`${t("Open in Deal Workspace")} · ${deal.accountName}`}` (keep the visible amount).

findings.state: Browser tab / history / bookmark title for every screen version
findings.problem: The area was renamed Getting to Signed (the page heading, palette and navigation say so), but the browser tab still says 'Negotiation'.

findings.state: Workstreams, stakeholders, security coverage, signature plan and target date for every deal
findings.current: export const GTS_KEY = "gtmos_getting_to_signed_v1"; (saved with localStorage only)
findings.problem: The default screen's entire model is stored only in this browser's localStorage; lib/cloud-persistence.ts syncs only the legacy negotiations and lessons bag. A seller who opens the workspace on another device, or a hire inheriting it, sees none of the workstreams or the signature plan, while the rest of the area (and Settings' 'saved to the cloud' statement) implies cloud persistence.
findings.governing: comprehension principle (save-state trust, CLAUDE.md Part III §4 lever 5); owner requirement 7 (persistence across handoffs)
findings.proposed: No copy change makes this accurate on its own. OWNER DECISION: add the per-deal SignedState to the cloud bag (e.g. a `gts` map inside the existing studio_artifacts 'negotiation.workspace' row via negotiation-bridge.ts) so it syncs like the rest of the area.

retained.why: Approved Batch 02 replacement B2-X-084 verbatim; the link goes to Call in a Favor with the deal preselected. Understandable as a request for help; destination not named but a link.
Implements the Batch 02 'GAP' requirement as a plain label between customer request and proposed position.

retained.text: SOC 2, the subprocessor list, penetration-test material, and the DPA may already answer part of the questionnaire.
retained.why: Hedged with 'may' and shown as guidance; the app does not assert the seller holds these documents — availability is only what the user toggles under 'Security documents available', and coverage numbers are user-entered (questions total / answered by existing documents / saved answers).

retained.text: Getting to Signed helps you prepare for procurement, finance, legal, security, and commercial negotiation before the conversation happens.
retained.why: Rendered only by WayfinderBar (src/components/navigation.tsx:195), which is used by the previous screen version (ds/NegotiationDS.tsx), whose content is exactly that preparation; the v4 default screen does not render WayfinderBar.
